why: Four lanes today delivered packets that passed all nine completeness counters and were still wrong on the page. The counters are not broken; they answer the questions they were built to answer. These are the questions they do not ask. Every one was found by reading the delivered PDF bytes rather than the build report, and every one would have reached a participant.
howEveryOneOfTheseWasFound: By diffing the delivered pages against the pinned source, or by reading the produced PDF at appearance level. Not one was found by a counter, a build report or a self-check.

defects.what: The build wrote four values onto a petition sworn before a notary that its own field map declared blank: the legal name on both lines of 'current name, previous names, and all aliases', and the current address on both lines of 'all addresses since the offense'.
defects.whyItMatters: A legal name alone asserts there are no aliases. One address written twice asserts a residence history. Both are sworn statements about the participant's life, invented by a builder.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: The completeness contract reads the field map, and the map was honest about its intent. The finalizer wrote something else. Nothing compared the two.
defects.theFix: A gate that stops when the finalizer's writes and the map's writes disagree. PF04 added one to its own scripts and tested it by removing a refusal to confirm it fires.
defects.whoElseIsExposed: Every family on the finalizeOfficialForm path.

defects.foundBy: PF21, nd-regular-pardon-set -- and it is the SECOND independent instance of this class today, after PF04's wv_conv_nonviolent_felony-set
defects.what: On an 8-page 229-field pardon application, 28 blanks bind a participant fact while describing someone else. NameRow1..7 bind participant.full_legal_name and are the VICTIM NAME COLUMN of item 3. Left alone, the packet would have named the applicant as the victim of their own offence, seven times. AddressRow and Telephone NumberRow are the EMPLOYER's, item 11. City or CountyRow1..9 are the offence venue, not where the participant lives.
defects.whyItMatters: This is the same class as the West Virginia aliases defect and it is not a coincidence. The shared name channel binds a field by the SHAPE OF ITS NAME rather than by whose fact it holds, so any form whose field names are autogenerated -- this one was produced by Acrobat PDFMaker 11 for Word, which is why the names are odd -- will attract a participant's data into columns about victims, employers, courts and third parties.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: Every one of those blanks is a real terminal field expecting a name or an address. Filling it is a write inside a measured box with a plausible value. Nothing counts whose fact a field holds.
defects.theFix: Decide each binding by ROLE, refusing every field whose printed context names a different party, and confirm the delivered tables are empty in the output bytes. PF21 refused all 28 and confirmed all five tables delivered empty.
defects.whoElseIsExposed: Every family on the shared name channel, which is most of them. Two of the two families examined for it today were affected.

defects.what: On a 37-row charge table, 52 of 111 cells carry an AcroForm index that disagrees with the row number printed beside them. Printed row 5 is TextField3[6] / DropDownList1[9] / DateField1[7]; printed row 13 is TextField3[12] / DropDownList1[1] / DateField1[12].
defects.whyItMatters: A builder that derives a row number from a field index labels a cell for one charge and places it on another charge's line, on a petition signed under a perjury warning.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: The cell count is right and the label count is right. Both counters read clean while every affected charge is on the wrong line.
defects.theFix: Resolve each cell's row by geometry against the printed number, and refuse the build if a cell matches none or more than one.
defects.whoElseIsExposed: Any family whose official form carries a numbered table. An index-derived row number is not evidence.

defects.what: 'Charge Date of Nolle Prosequi or' extracts as one line, which reads as though the date column is in the middle. By item x-position the middle heading is 'State Whether the Court Entered a Nolle Prosequi or Dismissed the Charge' and the right one is 'Date of Nolle Prosequi or Dismissal'. Confirmed independently by the middle widget's own option list: Nolle Prosequi / Dismissed.
defects.whyItMatters: The naive reading tells a participant to write a date in the box asking which disposition the court entered.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: Nothing counts whether a heading was read in the right order.
defects.theFix: Read headings by x-position, and cross-check against the widget's own option list where it has one.

defects.what: A proposed order recited its legal-design record's mandate sentences verbatim, two of which are analysis addressed to the builder -- one literally saying the packet copy must not tell a participant the order is guaranteed. Separately, a machine vocabulary of eligible dispositions printed as a bullet list on the face of a motion, and a memo's internal component note printed at the foot of a composed form.
defects.whyItMatters: A proposed order handed to a judge reciting instructions addressed to its own builder is not a filing.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: The text is present, non-empty, inside its write box and quoted verbatim from a controlling record. Every check passes.
defects.theFix: Filings recite statute citations and rule text only. The record's own words belong in the guide, labelled as internal record text.

defects.what: addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes was a hardcoded literal 0 while a real reading of the same quantity sat beside it under flattenedShowTextGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes. The packets published a zero where they held a measurement. Real values were 627/1007 and 887/1159.
defects.whyItMatters: A zero that was never measured is indistinguishable, downstream, from a zero that was.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: The field was present and numeric.
defects.whoElseIsExposed: scripts/build-census-v1-ne-seal-pardoned-set.mjs carries the same pattern and has not been repaired.

defects.what: nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes reads zero with the defect present when the stray ink draws at a widget's own rect -- the CR-180 privacy banner draws at the Warning pushbutton's rect, which IS in the census, so it lands inside a measured box.
defects.whyItMatters: That counter's zero is being trusted as evidence that nothing strayed. For this class of defect it is not evidence of anything.
defects.theFix: The reading that has teeth here is flattenedControlChromeGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes: 126 glyphs at 4 widgets on the pre-repair bytes, 0 now.

defects.what: al-felony-nonconviction-90-set and al-pardoned-felony-set render byte-identical page images to each other. Their PDFs share a 577-byte prefix and differ only in the /Title metadata string. The pardoned family ticks zero of the eight eligibility boxes its own CR-65 Section V requires.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: Every gate in this factory asks its question of one family at a time. Nothing had ever compared two families to each other.
defects.theFix: scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/verify-no-cloned-family-packets.mjs, and its finding at CLONED_FAMILY_PACKETS.json: 14 cloned deliverable groups.

defects.foundBy: PFD flattener-geometry lane, al-pardoned-felony-set and al-felony-nonconviction-90-set
defects.what: ISO 32000-1 7.9.5 lets a rectangle be written with ANY two diagonally opposite corners and requires a consumer to normalise it in situ. pdf-lib normalises nothing: getRectangle() returns the raw first corner as the origin with a signed height, and PDFForm.flatten() emits `q 1 0 0 1 x1 y1 cm /FlatWidget Do Q` -- so a widget whose /Rect is stored inverted has its appearance stamped exactly one box height away from the control the form draws. On Alabama's CR-65, page 3 check box Check Box10.2 carries /Rect [45.317 623.137 56.5341 608.779] and its unticked /N /Off appearance is `1 g / 0 0 11.2171 14.3578 re / f` -- a WHITE FILLED RECTANGLE. Delivered, it painted 14.358pt high across the word "expired" in the quashed-indictment ground's own printed sentence, "expired or the prosecuting agency confirms that the charge or charges will not be refiled." Measured at 300 dpi on al-pardoned-felony-set's delivered canonical page 3: 208 dark pixels in the pinned source over that region against 10 delivered, 198 lost, and every one of the 198 pixels page 3 lost was inside it.
defects.whyItMatters: The box is white and opaque, so it does not add ink -- it REMOVES it, from the text of a statutory eligibility ground on a sworn petition. A participant reading the delivered filing sees a word gouged out of the ground they are being asked to certify. Eight Alabama families bind this source.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: The appearance draws no glyphs, so nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes is honestly zero; and the stream is byte-identical to the form's own /AP, so stroke-only source accounting returns MATCHED -- 160 of 160 across both fixtures, 0 unmatched. Both byte tools called the family clean. It is also invisible to the write-box reading when that reading is taken against the delivered placement rather than the source form's own /Rect, because a misplaced appearance is always inside its own misplacement.
defects.theFix: Normalise the widget /Rect in situ before anything reads it -- appearance regeneration, the 12.5.5 fit and flatten's own translate all resolve the rectangle through the same accessor, so one correction serves all three. scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs exports normalizeInvertedWidgetRectangles for that; it is opt-in per caller (normalizeInvertedWidgetRects) on the same reasoning as the other flags there. It is NOT fitAppearancesToRect: measured on CR-65, that flag corrects four appearances and Check Box10.2 is not among them, because its BBox already maps onto its rectangle with the identity.
defects.whoElseIsExposed: Measured, not guessed. scripts/rcap-official-forms/scan-inverted-widget-rects.mjs walked custody by content digest: 46 inverted-rect widgets in 13 held AcroForm PDFs, out of 13,023 widgets in 245 forms. Only ONE paints today (CR-65's Check Box10.2) -- the other 45 are empty text fields and unticked boxes whose /N carries no painting operator, which is exactly how CR-65's looked before a family wrote near it. Two of the 13 forms are bound by a family receipt today: Alabama CR-65 (8 families) and Indiana CCA-XP-0220-7010 (in_conviction_felony-set, 6 inverted widgets). The rest -- IN CCA-SECTION1-INSERTS (11), VT 200-00631 (5), MO FI-05 (5), VA CC-1201 (4), IN ConvictionPetitionOrder (4), MO CR300 (2), VA CC-1203-B (2), MO mistaken-identity (2), WV SCA-C906 (2), WV SCA-C907 (1), VA cc1473 (1) -- are held but not yet digest-bound, and carry the same defect the day a family binds and writes them. Offsets run 9.84 to 17.28pt; every one is y-inverted and none is x-inverted.

defects.what: FIX132 repaired both Indiana families and reported 'Removed ink not accounted to a selection widget: 0'. The delivered pages are in fact missing 27,981 dark pixels of the source's own ink: the FACTS offence grid prints twelve writing rules in rows A to D in the source and none in the delivered page, and Exhibit A's seven-row disposition table delivers as a bare grid with every rule gone -- while the participant guide names nineteen boxes in that table for them to fill in by hand.
defects.whyItMatters: Over-suppression is the defect that erases what the court prints, and the directional pixel difference is the ONLY check the factory has for it. A rendering choice silently disables that check and returns the answer the lane hoped for. Two families shipped a published zero over 27,981 px of erased ink, and MASTER_QUEUE carried visualDefects 0 and allNineCountersZero true for both.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: The source was rendered WITHOUT annotations. An AcroForm source keeps much of what the court prints inside widget /AP /N appearance streams; an annotation-free render never draws them, so the source render is missing exactly the ink whose absence from the delivered page the diff is meant to detect. Both sides are blank in the same places and the difference is zero. No counter is involved and no counter could be: the measurement was blind before the arithmetic began.
defects.howItWasProved: VF26 rendered the PRE-repair inserts from 4316fccf2^ and got the identical removal counts, 10,372 dark pixels on insert page 1 and 4,151 on page 4. A repair that changes nothing about a number has not addressed what the number measures. Separately, 2,632 of the removed pixels fall outside every source widget rect, so even the narrower claim the commit actually made -- removed ink 'not accounted to a selection widget' -- is false on the bytes it shipped.
defects.theFix: Render the pinned source with annotations drawn, and prove the render before trusting any zero it produces: pick a widget known to carry visible ink in its /AP /N and confirm it appears in the source render. If the source render shows a bare grid where a viewer shows ruled rows, the render is wrong and every zero it produced is worthless. Report removed pixels per page and state how the source was rendered; a count without that sentence is not a usable measurement.
defects.whatMakesItGeneral: Nothing about this is specific to Indiana or to FIX132. Every lane in this factory is instructed to measure in both directions against a render of the pinned source, and none of the briefs said how to render it. Any lane that reaches for an annotation-free render gets a zero it cannot distinguish from a correct one -- and byte accounting cannot cover for it, because byte accounting only asks whether a delivered stream exists in the source and is blind to over-suppression by construction.

defects.foundBy: FIX130, vt_exp_decriminalized-set and the three Vermont sealing families, 2026-09-10
defects.what: On Vermont form 600-00228 the page-1 expenses column was labelled one row out from field 50 down. The blank beside the printed word Clothing was disclosed as 'the unlabelled expense line printed left of Clothing', the blank beside Medical was disclosed as Clothing, and so on through Child Support, Auto Loan Payment, Property Taxes and Insurance -- until field 57, THE BLANK BESIDE 'Total Expenses', was disclosed as 'Other Expenses' with the what-to-write 'any other monthly expense'.
defects.whyItMatters: The participant is told to write one other expense on the line where the court asks for their total, on a declaration signed under penalty of perjury. Every disclosed label was a real printed caption on the same form and the count of labels was right; only the pairing was wrong.
defects.whyNoCounterSawIt: Nothing compares a caption to the geometry of the blank it names. The label count matched the blank count, every label existed on the page, no blank was undisclosed and no disclosure was orphaned -- so unclassifiedBlanks, knownRequiredFieldsMissing and requiredFactsNotCollected all read zero with the defect present on every copy.
defects.howItWasProved: Each widget rect was matched against the printed dollar run whose baseline falls inside it, and the result confirmed on a render of the source with every widget rectangle drawn and labelled. The same pass found field 35 named after a line 24pt above it, and the Vehicles headings split on the extraction rather than by x-position -- 'Make, Model' and 'Year / Fair Market Value' where the form prints 'Make, Model, Year' and 'Fair Market Value (FMV)'.
defects.theFix: Resolve a caption from the blank's own coordinates, not from reading order, and assert every label unique within form and page. Where the same words appear beside more than one blank, disambiguate by the printed row number found at that blank's own height and to its left -- never by AcroForm index.
defects.whatMakesItGeneral: The field map's own captionBasis asserted that 'every printed caption in this map was read from the official form's own content stream at the widget's coordinates.' It was not, and nothing tested the claim. A map that states its method is not evidence that it followed it. Two more traps sit beside this one on the same form: its /TU tooltips name the wrong field on eighteen widgets (seven read 'In Re:', eleven read 'DOB'), so tooltips are unusable as caption evidence; and at two blanks the printed page is genuinely ambiguous -- four label lines and two dollar runs, each run 5.4 and 5.3pt below the label above and 6.6 and 6.8pt above the label below -- where the right answer is to leave the pairing as committed and record the ambiguity rather than pick one.
defects.andAFullINDEPENDENTPASSSATONTOPOFIT: The claim ledger records lane VF03 returning PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT for vt_seal_dui-set at commit 7d2e1ba7b -- fifteen of fifteen obligations passed, all nine counters zero -- on the EXACT BYTES where field 57, the blank beside Total Expenses, was disclosed to the participant as 'Other Expenses' with the instruction to write any other monthly expense. The reading was not careless in any way a rule can name: every label was a real printed caption on the form, the label count matched the blank count, and nothing was orphaned. This is the clearest evidence in the factory that a complete fifteen-obligation pass does not reach a caption paired with the wrong blank, and that the remedy is a geometric test rather than a stricter reader.
defects.howTheGeometricTestIsBuilt: FIX130 built it twice, and says why: pair each widget rect with the printed dollar run whose baseline falls INSIDE its own rectangle and overlaps it in x; read the caption from printed items on that run's baseline band, inside that run's own COLUMN, with the column taken from the page's two printed headings by x-position and never from extraction order; refuse a widget with no such run or more than one rather than guessing. The first detector tested for an item whose whole text is '$' and silently orphaned four widgets, because the left income column encodes its marker as one item '$__'.

whatThisIsNot: Not a verdict on any family and not a promotion of anything. It is the list of questions the counters do not ask, kept in one place so a lane can check them deliberately instead of rediscovering them.
theOneRuleThatWouldHaveCaughtMostOfThese: Read the delivered PDF, not the build report. Every defect here was invisible to the report that described it.
howManyInstances: Two of these classes have now been found twice independently: a participant fact written into a field about someone else (WV, ND), and a hardcoded zero published where a real measurement sat beside it (MD, MO, and NE unrepaired). A third class is now measured across the whole held corpus rather than inferred: an inverted widget rectangle, 46 widgets in 13 forms, of which exactly one paints today.
